editing_rules: Never add a derived value (a ratio, percentage or difference) to this file. Add its inputs and let the renderer compute it.
Every figure needs source, asof and basis. If a figure has no citable source, set needs_source true and it will render with a visible 'source needed' chip.
Never present a count as 'number of hog farms' without stating the basis — permitted certificates of coverage, active permits, and facilities are three different counts in North Carolina.

permit_regime_warning.headline: Permit counts are not comparable across states.
permit_regime_warning.body: Large swine operations are permitted under fundamentally different instruments by state. Only Illinois and Oklahoma route most large swine operations through an NPDES permit. In Iowa, North Carolina, Indiana and Nebraska — and in the no-discharge tiers of Minnesota, Missouri and South Dakota — the default instrument is a STATE-only permit that produces no NPDES record and therefore no EPA ECHO entry. Roughly 62 to 74 percent of the national herd sits in those states. A choropleth built on EPA ECHO NPDES data shows Iowa, which holds about a third of all US hogs, as nearly empty. FAT therefore builds the base choropleth on USDA NASS inventory and treats permits as a separate, explicitly labeled categorical layer.
permit_regime_warning.correct_label_for_echo: facilities holding a federal NPDES CAFO permit

state_evidence.basis: The Iowa Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Animal Feeding Operations (AFO) geodatabase carries NPDESPermitIssueDate per facility. Swine facilities are those with any swine animal units recorded. Under Iowa law a totally roofed confinement is deemed non-discharging and needs no NPDES permit, which is why the confinement column is almost entirely empty.
state_evidence.caveat: The published geodatabase was last updated April 5, 2024 and covers facilities at 300 or more animal units, so smaller operations are out of scope.
state_evidence.internal_note: NPDESPermitIssueDate is a string field: missing values are the literal text NULL, not an empty field. A truthiness test on it reports 100% coverage. The Swine_* columns are ANIMAL UNITS, not head — they equal TotalAnimalUnitsByFacility exactly on pure-swine facilities.

Renderers must show those states as 'not separately published', never as zero, and must never distribute this figure across them.

all_swine_permits.basis: All records where DESC_ LIKE 'Swine%', any status.
all_swine_permits.label: All swine permits

all_active_permits.label: All active permits, every animal type

all_permits.basis: Every record in the layer, all animal types, any status.
all_permits.label: All permit records

deq_reported_swine_facilities.basis: Swine facilities as stated in DEQ's statutory annual report to the General Assembly, FY2023-24.
deq_reported_swine_facilities.label: DEQ annual report — swine facilities

deq_reported_all_operations.basis: All permitted animal operations, DEQ annual report FY2023-24.
deq_reported_all_operations.label: DEQ annual report — all operations

reconciliation_gap.note: DEQ's own report count (2,047 swine facilities) and its own GIS layer (2,222 swine records) differ by about 175, and DEQ publishes no reconciliation. Likely causes: superseded certificates retained as rows, digester certificates issued alongside a base certificate for the same farm, and facilities carrying more than one animal-type record. FAT has now done that deduplication: the 2,146 active swine records resolve to 1,987 distinct permit numbers, which lands between DEQ's two published figures and is the number its own caveat was pointing at.

inspectors.basis: DEQ staff inspecting animal feeding operations. These staff split time across multiple programs, so the full-time-equivalent figure is lower than 14.

operations_covered.basis: All permitted operations those 14 inspectors cover: 2,200 swine CAFOs plus 218 cattle operations plus 18 wet-litter poultry farms. This is the correct denominator for a per-inspector ratio — the earlier 157:1 figure divided swine facilities alone by 14 and therefore understated the load.

nc_enforcement.ratio_note: Compute the ratio at render as operations_covered / inspectors. Do not type it. Depending on which source supplies the denominator the ratio ranges from about 157:1 (DEQ's FY2023-24 all-operations count) to about 177:1 (the layer's active permit count); the displayed figure must state which denominator it used.

complaints_investigated.basis: Complaints about CAFOs investigated by NC DEQ, November 2018 through the end of 2025. This is a DEQ complaint count, NOT an EPA ECHO violation count, and it is not comparable to ECHO figures for other states.

violation_rate.basis: Violations found in approximately one in five investigated complaints.

response_deadline_days.basis: Under a 2017 settlement DEQ must visit the CAFO within five days of a complaint unless there is an immediate threat to human health or the environment.

nc_enforcement.confidentiality_note: The substance of complaints remains confidential, and a violation enters the public record only if an inspector independently verifies it. Waste-removal violations are difficult to establish if an inspector arrives after the 15-day legal deadline.
nc_enforcement.unpermitted_gap_note: Poultry operations using dry-litter disposal require no permit and receive no routine inspection, so the true number of animal feeding operations in North Carolina is not knowable from permit data.

nc_legal_authority.headline: The enforcement gap is legal as well as numerical.
nc_legal_authority.body: Three separate disclosure and enforcement mechanisms covering North Carolina swine operations have closed since October 2025. Adding inspectors would not restore any of them: there is no annual operations report to inspect against, no points mechanism escalating to permit revocation, and no federal duty to report air releases of ammonia or hydrogen sulfide.

mechanisms.name: Annual operations report
mechanisms.detail: A two-page annual summary of animal numbers, lagoons and manure application acreage. Struck as a rule that was never promulgated under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).

mechanisms.name: Phosphorus Loss Assessment Tool analysis
mechanisms.detail: Phosphorus Loss Assessment Tool (PLAT) analysis on high-phosphorus fields with mitigation required at specified ratings. Struck on the same grounds.

mechanisms.name: Floodplain groundwater monitoring wells
mechanisms.detail: Monitoring wells for waste storage structures sited in the 100-year floodplain. Struck on the same grounds.

mechanisms.name: Violation points system (N.C.G.S. 143-215.6E)
mechanisms.detail: Enacted in 1997. Three significant violations within five years triggered mandatory permit revocation. Repealed outright after 29 years.

mechanisms.name: Air-release reporting under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA)
mechanisms.detail: Congress exempted air emissions from animal waste at a farm from CERCLA section 103 reporting.

mechanisms.name: Air-release reporting under the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA)
mechanisms.detail: EPA extended the exemption to EPCRA section 304. The challenge was decided for EPA on August 7, 2025 and is on appeal in the D.C. Circuit, No. 25-5354.

mechanisms.name: General permit renewal
mechanisms.detail: DEQ ran a full 2024 renewal with a comment period and four public hearings but never issued the permits. The General Assembly extended the 2019 and 2022 permits to September 30, 2028. The renewal was the natural vehicle for re-promulgating the struck conditions.

mechanisms.name: Rulemaking to restore the struck conditions
mechanisms.detail: As of September 2026 the Environmental Management Commission's pending-rules docket contains no animal waste, phosphorus or floodplain groundwater rulemaking.

open_proceeding.name: EPA Title VI Complaint 05RNO-21-R4
open_proceeding.detail: Challenges DEQ's March 2021 issuance of four swine digester permits in Duplin and Sampson Counties, where populations of color are 54 to 76 percent of residents within one mile. Accepted January 13, 2022, tolled since October 2022, still open with no published finding.

state_enforcement.note: One entry per state in the top ten by hog inventory, other than North Carolina, whose fuller record lives in nc_enforcement, nc_facility_counts and nc_legal_authority. A metric with value null and not_published_by means the agency publishes no such figure; the proxy string says what the closest public evidence is. Every figure here is all-species unless scope is swine. Ratios (NPDES share, operations per inspector) are computed by the renderer, never typed.
state_enforcement.ranking_basis: Top ten states by all hogs and pigs on hand, USDA NASS Quarterly Hogs and Pigs, September 1, 2026. The inventory figures displayed come from the states block of this file, which carries the June 2026 quarter.

scope_copy.headline: Enforcement is a state-by-state record, and this page builds it one state at a time
scope_copy.body: Most large hog operations in the United States hold a state permit rather than a federal National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit, so they never appear in the EPA's Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO) database. There is no national enforcement record for hogs. Each state's record has to be assembled from its own regulator's files, and what those files contain ranges from an annual inspection table to nothing at all. North Carolina, where FAT first did this work, remains the most detailed entry. The other nine states are the rest of the top ten by hog inventory. Where a regulator does not publish a figure, this page says so: the gap is part of the finding.

states.name: Iowa
states.program: Animal Feeding Operations (AFO) section, Environmental Services Division; on-site inspections by six regional Environmental Field Offices.
states.permit_regime_text: Large hog confinements are regulated under a state-only regime: a DNR construction permit at 1,000 or more animal units, scored through the county "Master Matrix", plus a Manure Management Plan (MMP) for confinements above 500 animal units that is updated annually. Under Iowa law a totally roofed confinement is deemed non-discharging and needs no NPDES permit, so almost no hog confinement holds one; Iowa's NPDES CAFO permits are overwhelmingly held by open cattle feedlots.
states.key_term: In Iowa the regulator is the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and the plan it reviews is the Manure Management Plan (MMP).

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.basis: Unique active swine facilities in the DNR Animal Feeding Operations geodatabase (facilities at 300 or more animal units with any swine recorded), deduplicated by FAT. Of these, 37 record an NPDES permit issue date.
swine_operations.label: Swine facilities in the DNR database

regulated_operations.basis: More than 8,000 active Manure Management Plans on file with DNR, all species, per a June 2025 records request. DNR's database lists fewer than 11,000 animal feeding operations in total; aerial-imagery mapping published in July 2026 counted 15,309, of which 10,172 were hog facilities.
regulated_operations.label: Active manure management plans

inspectors.proxy: The AFO section has five full-time employees plus some field officers, with no budget or staffing increase in nearly a decade; AFO enforcement funding has been $1.32 million a year since 2014.

inspection_policy.basis: No statutory inspection-frequency requirement applies to confinements. DNR's inspection standard operating procedure covers only NPDES-permitted sites. Administrative penalties are capped at $10,000 per violation; recent hog-manure spill orders have typically been $5,000.

inspections_per_year.basis: On-site animal feeding operation inspections DNR reported for 2025, all species. Swine-only inspections are not published.
inspections_per_year.label: On-site AFO inspections, 2025

complaints_per_year.proxy: DNR does not publish an annual complaint count. A Food & Water Watch review of DNR records found 179 manure discharges to Iowa waters between 2013 and 2023.

violations_per_year.basis: About 50 notices of violation arising from the 2025 inspections, all species, per a DNR spokesperson. DNR also reported 97 manure-management-plan and 62 prohibited-discharge enforcement actions since 2020.
violations_per_year.label: Notices of violation, 2025

states.publication_note: Iowa publishes inspection and violation counts only when asked by reporters; there is no annual enforcement report, and roughly half of the manure management plans exist only on paper.

developments.detail: Environmental Working Group imagery mapping found 15,309 animal feeding operations against fewer than 11,000 in DNR records; large CAFOs grew from 3,936 (2019) to 4,444 (2025). DNR said its database cannot capture confinements below the reporting threshold.

Inside Climate News found roughly half of the 8,000-plus manure management plans are paper-only; DNR estimated two years and $85,000 to digitize them. State Auditor Rob Sand proposed a uniform online form and public application records.
Food & Water Watch called for NPDES permits for large operations and inspection of one-fifth of permitted sites each year; Iowa law keeps manure-application records confidential.

states.name: Minnesota
states.program: Feedlot Program, with staff in six regional offices; about 50 livestock-dense counties run delegated County Feedlot Programs through County Feedlot Officers.
states.permit_regime_text: Nearly every feedlot at 50 or more animal units must register; feedlots at 1,000 or more animal units need either a State Disposal System (SDS) permit or an NPDES permit. Minnesota is unusual in that most large feedlots, swine included, take the NPDES general permit rather than the state-only SDS permit, so a majority of large hog operations here do have a federal record. Smaller operations need a short-form construction permit only when they build.
states.key_term: In Minnesota the regulator is the Minnesota Pollution Control Agency (MPCA); its state-only permit is the State Disposal System (SDS) permit.

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.basis: Unique active swine operations in the MPCA feedlot extract, deduplicated by FAT. Of these, 617 hold an NPDES permit and 186 an SDS permit only; 4,752 state no permit, most of them below the permit threshold.
swine_operations.label: Swine operations in the MPCA feedlot extract

regulated_operations.basis: About 18,000 registered feedlots of all species, of which roughly 1,000 to 1,200 are large enough to need an SDS or NPDES permit.
regulated_operations.label: Registered feedlots

inspectors.proxy: MPCA does not publish a statewide inspector count. A 2023 fiscal note estimated four full-time staff for 660 inspections, about ten staff-hours each; county reports note staffing gaps and state funding held at early-2020 levels.

inspection_policy.basis: Delegated counties must inspect at least 7 percent of registered feedlots each year, at least half of them as compliance inspections, to earn performance credits. Permitted sites self-inspect weekly or monthly and file an annual report by March 1.

inspections_per_year.proxy: No statewide inspection total is published; each delegated county reports its own. Goodhue County, for example, reported 67 to 69 inspections in 2025, a 9.2 percent rate against the 7 percent minimum.

complaints_per_year.proxy: Counties must keep complaint logs and refer serious complaints to MPCA, but no statewide complaint count is published.

violations_per_year.proxy: MPCA publishes semiannual all-media enforcement summaries without a feedlot total. In the first half of 2024, 4 of 100 cases were feedlot violations, totalling $12,600 in penalties, including $4,200 against Wakefield Pork Inc.

states.publication_note: Minnesota is the one top-ten state where the permit instrument is published per operation, so the federal-record gap can be counted rather than estimated. Inspection and complaint counts, by contrast, are scattered across county reports.

developments.detail: MPCA finalized revised feedlot general permits (SDS effective June 1, 2025; NPDES effective February 1, 2026) adding nitrogen-practice rules in vulnerable groundwater areas, winter application bans, manure-recipient recordkeeping and a mandatory online nutrient management tool.
A court order in a nitrate lawsuit over karst and Central Sands groundwater gave MPCA and the Department of Agriculture one year to show current rules protect drinking water.

MPCA opened rulemaking to amend the 25-year-old chapter 7020 feedlot rules; the comment period closed with about 7,500 pages of comments, and environmental groups are seeking operating permits for the 374 operations just under the 1,000-animal-unit threshold. Rulemaking is expected to run into 2027.

states.name: Illinois
states.regulator: Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA) and Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA)
states.program: Illinois EPA Bureau of Water issues NPDES CAFO permits and conducts inspections; IDOA's Livestock Management Facilities Program handles siting, construction, lagoon registration and waste management plans.
states.permit_regime_text: Illinois has no state operating permit for hog confinements. New facilities file a Notice of Intent to Construct with IDOA under the Livestock Management Facilities Act; lagoons are registered; facilities at 1,000 or more animal units need a waste management plan, self-certified below 5,000 animal units. NPDES permits are required only for CAFOs that discharge, so almost no Illinois hog operation holds one, and Illinois EPA has acknowledged it has no comprehensive inventory of CAFOs.
states.key_term: In Illinois the regulators are the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA) and the Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA), under the Livestock Management Facilities Act (LMFA).

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.proxy: Neither agency publishes a count of hog operations. The Illinois Environmental Council states 680 CAFO applications were approved and built over the past decade and that IDOA has never denied a notice of intent.

regulated_operations.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of all species as reported to EPA, the only official count. A 2010 EPA Region 5 review estimated about 500 large CAFOs, and in 2017 an Illinois EPA official told a Senate subcommittee the agency still did not know how many large hog confinements exist.
regulated_operations.label: CAFOs reported to EPA

inspectors.proxy: The last official figure is from EPA Region 5's 2010 review: seven Bureau of Water staff with CAFO permitting and inspection as collateral duties.

inspection_policy.basis: Illinois EPA's stated goal is one inspection of each permitted CAFO per five-year permit term, which EPA found was not met in 2010. IDOA says lagoons at facilities of 1,000 or more animal units are inspected annually. Illinois EPA has no administrative penalty authority; cases go to the Attorney General or the Pollution Control Board.

inspections_per_year.proxy: No annual inspection count is published. EPA's 2010 review found about three-quarters of livestock inspections were complaint-driven.

complaints_per_year.proxy: No complaint count is published. EPA's 2010 review cited more than 200 complaints a year at the Peoria office alone, about 37 percent of them livestock-related.

violations_per_year.proxy: No count is published. Enforcement appears case by case at the Pollution Control Board, such as PCB 2026-033 (October 2025) against Paragon Pork, a 5,000-hog farrow-to-wean site, over a 2020 land-application discharge and a 1,447-fish kill.

states.publication_note: Illinois is the state in this set with the thinnest record: no inventory of hog operations, no inspection or complaint counts, and no administrative penalties. The only enforcement visible to the public is what the Attorney General files.

developments.detail: Attorney General Raoul filed PCB 2026-033 against Paragon Pork and its applicator over a 2020 manure discharge and fish kill at an unpermitted large CAFO, seeking $50,000 per violation.

SB 2331 to 2333 would have added county-board notice, two-mile setbacks and water-impact surveys to the Livestock Management Facilities Act; referred to Assignments and not moved, with Farm Bureau, Illinois Pork Producers and Illinois Beef opposed.
Illinois EPA reissued general permit ILA01 after the 2009 permit lapsed in 2014; further Part 502 amendments are before the Pollution Control Board in docket R25-23.

states.name: Indiana
states.program: Confined Feeding Program, Office of Land Quality, under the Confined Feeding Control Law (Indiana Code 13-18-10).
states.permit_regime_text: Any operation with 600 or more swine is a Confined Feeding Operation (CFO) and must hold an IDEM approval before building or operating. Operations with 2,500 or more swine over 55 pounds are tracked as CAFOs by size but are still permitted under the state CFO rule unless they discharge. NPDES coverage is effectively unused: EPA lists Indiana with zero NPDES-permitted CAFOs, so IDEM's "CAFO" label means size class, not a federal permit.
states.key_term: In Indiana the regulator is the Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) and the state permit is the Confined Feeding Operation (CFO) approval.

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.proxy: IDEM's annual report does not split its 1,647 permitted operations by species. The IndianaMap Confined Feeding Operations layer carries an animal-type field and is the closest proxy.

regulated_operations.basis: Operations subject to permitting and inspection in fiscal 2025: 789 CFOs plus 658 large CAFO-size operations, all species. Down from 1,730 in fiscal 2022.
regulated_operations.label: Permitted CFOs and CAFOs, FY2025

inspectors.proxy: A December 2024 fiscal note said annual inspections would require up to six additional inspectors; IDEM testified it inspects about 20 percent of CFOs each year.

inspection_policy.basis: Routine inspection roughly once every five years plus a first-year inspection. Since Senate Enrolled Act 193 (2025), IDEM must inspect each CFO within 45 days of initial approval and within 90 days of renewal, and may make unannounced complaint inspections; the bill's original annual-inspection mandate was removed.

inspections_per_year.basis: All CFO and CAFO inspections in fiscal 2025: 329 routine, 16 complaint, 26 follow-up, 82 construction and 35 exit or closure, plus other. All species.
inspections_per_year.label: Inspections, FY2025

complaints_per_year.proxy: Complaints received are not reported; 16 complaint-based inspections were made in fiscal 2025 (15 in fiscal 2022).

violations_per_year.basis: Violations cited in fiscal 2025: 37 at CFOs and 27 at large CAFO-size operations, led by land application (26) and operational standards (20). Formal enforcement actions are not counted in the report.
violations_per_year.label: Violations cited, FY2025

states.publication_note: Indiana is one of only two states in this set that publishes an annual inspection and violation table for its livestock program. It is also the only one with zero NPDES-permitted CAFOs, so none of its 1,647 permitted operations appears in EPA ECHO.

developments.detail: Senate Enrolled Act 193 (P.L. 192-2025) added inspections within 45 days of approval and 90 days of renewal and allowed unannounced complaint inspections, after Farm Bureau, Indiana Pork and the poultry association stripped the annual-inspection requirement.
House Enrolled Act 1355 added pre-application meetings, fee refunds when IDEM misses its 90-day deadline, and a bar on retroactive requirements for approved infrastructure during expansions.
In fiscal 2024 IDEM received 50 CFO approval applications, issued 46 and denied none.

states.name: Nebraska
states.regulator: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (DWEE)
states.program: Livestock Waste Control Program, Livestock and Agriculture Section, Water Quality Division (Title 130). Renamed from the Department of Environment and Energy (NDEE) by LB 317 in 2025.
states.permit_regime_text: Nebraska runs a dual system. A non-expiring state Construction and Operating Permit is required for any operation DWEE determines needs waste-control facilities; an NPDES permit is "generally required" for large and medium CAFOs that discharge or propose to. Unlike Indiana or Iowa, a sizeable share of Nebraska's large CAFOs do carry NPDES coverage, mostly cattle feedlots under the cattle general permit; the draft 2027-2032 reissuance would extend general coverage to all CAFO types and hold new swine CAFOs to zero production-area discharge.
states.key_term: In Nebraska the regulator is the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (DWEE), until 2025 the Department of Environment and Energy (NDEE).

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.proxy: DWEE describes "thousands" of animal feeding operations but publishes no species breakdown on its website; the livestock tables are in its annual report to the Legislature.

regulated_operations.proxy: No current total of permitted livestock operations is published online. EPA's count of 1,228 medium and large CAFOs reported by the state is the closest proxy; EPA cut that figure from 1,555 a year earlier without explanation.

inspectors.proxy: Agency-wide authorized staffing was 273 full-time equivalents at the start of fiscal 2024 and 268 at the end; the livestock share is not published.

inspection_policy.basis: DWEE states facilities are inspected every 18 to 24 months, if not more often, with an initial inspection before construction and a post-construction inspection within 30 days. It reports an average of 50 days to issue a livestock permit against a 110-day statutory limit.

inspections_per_year.basis: Average of 7,833 animal feeding operation inspections DWEE reported for 2014 through 2022, all species, with a stated 96 percent compliance rate. No annual figure is published; the average is computed from the nine-year total.
inspections_per_year.label: Inspections per year, 2014-2022 average

complaints_per_year.proxy: No livestock complaint count is published; the agency logged 325 citizen complaints across all programs in fiscal 2024.

violations_per_year.proxy: Letters of non-compliance are not counted publicly. Formal Livestock Waste Control enforcement orders listed on the agency site: 4 in 2024, 2 in 2025 and 1 so far in 2026, every one a cattle feedlot; no swine order was found.

states.publication_note: Nebraska's enforcement record is visible only as a cumulative inspection total and a handful of formal orders. LB 1048, introduced at the Governor's request in 2026, would eliminate the annual Livestock Waste Management Act cost report, one of the few public windows on program capacity.

developments.detail: Draft NPDES general permit NEG022000 for 2027-2032 was released for comment, extending general coverage to all CAFO types.
LB 1048 would change or eliminate state reporting requirements, including the Livestock Waste Management Act annual cost report.

LB 317 renamed the Department of Environment and Energy as the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment; conforming Title 130 amendments were heard by the Environmental Quality Council in June 2026.

states.name: Missouri
states.program: Water Protection Program, Division of Environmental Quality; CAFO permitting unit, with compliance monitoring by regional offices and referral to the Compliance and Enforcement Section.
states.permit_regime_text: Class I CAFOs (1,000 or more animal units; 2,500 or more swine over 55 pounds) need a Missouri State Operating Permit. Two master general permits apply: MO-G010000, an NPDES permit allowing discharge only in a 25-year, 24-hour storm, and MO-GS10000, a state no-discharge permit that most swine operations use. Class IA operations (7,000 or more animal units, which includes the Smithfield complexes) must hold site-specific NPDES permits. Class II operations of 300 to 999 animal units are unpermitted unless designated.
states.key_term: In Missouri the regulator is the Department of Natural Resources (MoDNR); its state-only instrument is the no-discharge general permit MO-GS10000.

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.proxy: MoDNR publishes a permit search and map but no species tally. Eighteen Class IA operations, mostly Smithfield hog complexes, hold site-specific NPDES permits.

regulated_operations.basis: Permitted Class I CAFOs of all species as reported to EPA. MoDNR itself publishes no total.
regulated_operations.label: Permitted Class I CAFOs

inspectors.proxy: No inspector count is published for the CAFO program.

inspection_policy.basis: Section 640.750 of the Revised Statutes requires at least one on-site DNR inspection each quarter of every Class IA facility. No statutory frequency applies to Class IB or IC operations.

inspections_per_year.proxy: No CAFO inspection total is published. The statute implies about 72 required Class IA inspections a year (18 facilities, quarterly) plus regional-office visits; facility-level actions appear in monthly Clean Water enforcement reports and the MoCWIS database.

complaints_per_year.proxy: Concerns are filed through an online form; no CAFO complaint tally is published.

violations_per_year.proxy: No CAFO count is published. Monthly Clean Water enforcement reports list facility-level actions; one example is an $18,000 penalty against a Smithfield site for a roughly 300,000-gallon spill in 2022.

states.publication_note: Missouri publishes facility-level enforcement documents but no program-level counts, and since 2023 counties cannot regulate CAFOs more strictly than the state.

developments.detail: The Missouri Supreme Court unanimously upheld Senate Bill 391 (2019) and its 2021 amendment, voiding county health ordinances that are stricter than, or different from, state CAFO rules.

Master general permits MO-G010000 and MO-GS10000 were reissued, expiring in February 2028, after a 2022 controversy over Smithfield's South Meadows site moving from a site-specific to a general permit.
Three petitions for rulemaking to amend 10 CSR 20-6.300, arising from southwest Missouri poultry permits, drew a DNR response to comments.

states.name: Ohio
states.regulator: Ohio Department of Agriculture (ODA), with Ohio Environmental Protection Agency (Ohio EPA) for NPDES
states.program: ODA Division of Livestock Environmental Permitting (DLEP) issues and inspects state permits; Ohio EPA issues the few NPDES CAFO permits, all of them individual.
states.permit_regime_text: Large hog farms (2,500 or more swine over 55 pounds) are Concentrated Animal Feeding Facilities (CAFFs) and need an ODA Permit to Install and a five-year Permit to Operate under Ohio Revised Code chapter 903. NPDES CAFO permits come only from Ohio EPA, only as individual permits, and only for the minority that discharge. EPA declined in 2022 to transfer NPDES CAFO permitting to ODA, so the split persists.
states.key_term: In Ohio the state regulator is the Ohio Department of Agriculture (ODA), whose permitted sites are Concentrated Animal Feeding Facilities (CAFFs); the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency (Ohio EPA) holds the NPDES program.

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.basis: Swine CAFFs of 265 permitted facilities in ODA's July 2021 presentation, the last species split found. ODA's annual reports since then give totals only.
swine_operations.label: Swine CAFFs (2021 split)

regulated_operations.basis: CAFFs operating under a Permit to Operate at the end of calendar 2024, all species (295 at the end of 2023).
regulated_operations.label: Permitted CAFFs, end of 2024

inspectors.basis: Division inspectors in July 2021, plus one vacancy and three engineers. ODA has not published a current headcount.
inspectors.label: Division inspectors (2021)

inspection_policy.basis: ODA policy is at least one routine inspection of every permitted CAFF each year, against a federal recommendation of once every five years.

inspections_per_year.basis: Routine inspections of permitted CAFFs in calendar 2024, all species (441 in 2023).
inspections_per_year.label: Routine inspections, 2024

complaints_per_year.basis: Complaint investigations at CAFFs in calendar 2024 (36 in 2023), plus 11 complaints about certified livestock managers. All species.
complaints_per_year.label: Complaint investigations, 2024

violations_per_year.proxy: The annual report gives no enforcement counts. ODA's tools are warning letters, notices of deficiency and director's orders; Ohio EPA's eDocument system holds the NPDES record.

states.publication_note: Ohio and Indiana are the only states in this set that publish annual inspection totals. Ohio also publishes complaint investigations, which makes its record the fullest after North Carolina's, though it stops short of counting violations.

developments.detail: EPA's Inspector General found EPA oversight gives reasonable assurance that Ohio's 20 NPDES CAFO nutrient management plans meet federal minimums, with no recommendations; it did not evaluate whether manure is applied as the plans say.

The Sixth Circuit ordered that Ohio agricultural associations including the Ohio Pork Council be admitted as intervenors in the Lucas County, Toledo and Environmental Law & Policy Center suit over EPA's approval of the Maumee River TMDL, which alleges at least 73 watershed CAFOs received no wasteload allocation.
EPA declined ODA's 2015 request to take over NPDES CAFO permitting from Ohio EPA.

states.name: South Dakota
states.regulator: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources (DANR)
states.program: Feedlot Permit Program, Division of Agriculture and Environmental Services.
states.permit_regime_text: Since 2007 every large CAFO (2,500 or more swine over 55 pounds) must hold coverage under DANR's General Water Pollution Control Permit for CAFOs, a combined NPDES and state general permit. DANR is splitting it into a five-year NPDES general permit and a ten-year state-only general permit; operators that do not discharge may choose the state-only version, so the share with a federal record is set to fall.
states.key_term: In South Dakota the regulator is the Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources (DANR).

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.basis: Permitted swine CAFOs holding 884,629 head on January 1, 2024, among 436 permitted facilities; a further 62 multi-animal facilities may include swine.
swine_operations.label: Permitted swine CAFOs

regulated_operations.basis: Permitted facilities of all species on January 1, 2024, a figure repeated in the Legislative Research Council's fiscal 2026 budget brief.
regulated_operations.label: Permitted facilities

inspectors.proxy: Division-wide staffing was 89.5 full-time equivalents in fiscal 2024 and 95.9 budgeted for fiscal 2025 across many programs; the feedlot share is not published.

inspection_policy.basis: DANR policy is to inspect larger operations at least once a year and other operations at least once every three years, plus a construction inspection and one within the first 18 months of operation.

inspections_per_year.proxy: No inspection count is published. The budget performance measure is the share of CAFOs in compliance: 99.7 percent in fiscal 2023 and 2024.

complaints_per_year.proxy: A complaint form exists; no tally is published.

violations_per_year.proxy: No count is published. The 99.7 percent compliance measure implies roughly one non-compliant facility among about 436.

states.publication_note: South Dakota publishes the best species breakdown of permitted operations in this set but no inspection, complaint or violation counts, and in 2025 the Legislature came within one committee vote of barring DANR from releasing the list of permitted CAFO locations.

developments.detail: DANR posted contested-case materials for splitting the CAFO general permit into a five-year NPDES permit and a ten-year state-only permit, as 2021 Senate Bill 52 allows.
Senate Bill 14 originally barred DANR from releasing an aggregated list of permitted CAFO locations; the House Agriculture committee deleted that section 13-0 before the bill was signed.
House Bill 1021 raised CAFO application and annual fees, phasing program revenue from about $97,000 to $705,000 a year.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.regulator: Oklahoma Department of Agriculture, Food and Forestry (ODAFF)
states.program: Agricultural Environmental Management Services (AEMS) division: swine feeding operations, CAFO, poultry and the Agricultural Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (AgPDES) programs.
states.permit_regime_text: Large hog farms are licensed by ODAFF as Licensed Managed Feeding Operations under the Oklahoma Swine Feeding Operations Act, at 1,000 swine animal units (2,500 swine over 55 pounds). ODAFF also holds EPA-delegated NPDES authority for agriculture (AgPDES, since 2013) and issues the AgPDES CAFO general permit OKG010000, from which new-source swine CAFOs are excluded and need individual permits. Most licensed swine operations rely on the state license alone; NPDES coverage is the minority.
states.key_term: In Oklahoma the regulator is the Department of Agriculture, Food and Forestry (ODAFF); its delegated federal program is the Agricultural Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (AgPDES).

epa_cafo_status.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of every species as reported by the state to EPA, and how many of them hold an NPDES permit. This is EPA's status report, not the ECHO database, and it is the only series published on the same definition for every state. It is not a count of hog farms.

swine_operations.proxy: ODAFF links to a list of permitted CAFOs but publishes no swine tally on its website; licensed-swine statistics appear in the monthly AEMS report in State Board of Agriculture packets.

regulated_operations.basis: Medium and large CAFOs of all species as reported to EPA. ODAFF publishes no total.
regulated_operations.label: CAFOs reported to EPA

inspectors.basis: AEMS division full-time equivalents in fiscal 2024 across swine, CAFO, poultry and pet-breeder programs (17.2 in fiscal 2023; 20.7 budgeted for fiscal 2025). The division web page names eight inspectors and two field supervisors.
inspectors.label: AEMS division staff (FTE), FY2024

inspection_policy.basis: The Swine Feeding Operations Act requires ODAFF to make at least one unannounced inspection each year of every licensed swine feeding operation (2 O.S. 20-14(A)).

inspections_per_year.proxy: No annual inspection count is published. The monthly AEMS report to the State Board of Agriculture includes inspection, complaint and technical-assistance counts but is not summarized annually.

complaints_per_year.proxy: Complaint investigations appear in the monthly AEMS board report only.

violations_per_year.proxy: No count is published. Individual enforcement stipulations appear on State Board of Agriculture agendas, for example four AEMS cases in July 2025 and four in April 2026.

states.publication_note: Oklahoma has the strictest inspection mandate in this set, one unannounced visit per licensed swine operation per year, but publishes no figure showing whether it is met, and in 2025 it repealed the violation points system that graded repeat offenders.

developments.detail: New swine rules took effect and revoked the violation points system (OAC 35:17-3-22), removing the graduated penalty scheme.
Revised Swine Feeding Operations Act and CAFO Act took effect.
AgPDES CAFO general permit OKG010000 reissued for 2023 to 2028.

moratorium.detail: Titled 'lagoon and sprayfield systems prohibited', but it bars a permit for such a system only unless the permit does not increase the farm's permitted capacity as measured by annual steady state live weight, or the system meets all five performance standards. The capacity-neutral exception is why existing lagoon farms renew indefinitely. The statute forecloses growth; it does not require replacement.

performance_standards: Eliminate the discharge of animal waste to surface water and groundwater through direct discharge, seepage, or runoff.
Substantially eliminate atmospheric emission of ammonia.
Substantially eliminate the emission of odor that is detectable beyond the boundaries of the parcel or tract of land on which the swine farm is located.
Substantially eliminate the release of disease-transmitting vectors and airborne pathogens.
Substantially eliminate nutrient and heavy metal contamination of soil and groundwater.

ownership.note: Foreign ownership is tracked as a category distinct from economic concentration.

parent_stake_pct.basis: Approximate WH Group holding after the September 2025 secondary offering.

listing.basis: Smithfield returned to US public markets on January 29, 2025. It is now a US-listed public company with a Chinese majority holder — a materially different structure from the wholly-owned subsidiary it was before 2025.

jbs.note: JBS N.V. became the parent in June 2025 (NYSE: JBS). Company-level share of U.S. hog slaughter is not published by USDA; national.cr4_packers gives the four-firm total.

integration.note: Vertical integration is loosening at the production end. A static 'about 90 percent contract' figure no longer describes the direction of travel.

smithfield_internal_production_head_m.basis: Internal hog production, FY2025, down from 14.6 million head in FY2024.

smithfield_internal_share_pct.basis: Share of hogs processed by the Fresh Pork segment that come from internal production.

nc_divestitures.detail: Contributed $3 million for a 25 percent minority interest in a Murphy Family Farms venture and sold approximately 150,000 sows and related inventories.
Contributed $450,000 for a 9 percent stake in VisionAg and divested approximately 28,000 sows and associated commercial hog inventories.

biogas.note: Digester permits layer a covered lagoon and gas line onto the existing lagoon and sprayfield rather than replacing it. No digester technology met North Carolina's environmentally superior technology standard on its own.

align_rng.structure: 50/50 joint venture between Smithfield Foods and Dominion Energy
align_rng.disclosure_note: Smithfield and Dominion have declined to disclose credit volumes or revenue, citing proprietary business information, and Align's certified carbon intensity score is not public.

lcfs_ci_range.basis: Certified California Air Resources Board (CARB) carbon intensity range for dairy and swine manure biomethane pathways, credited on an avoided-methane basis.

label_disclosure.headline: None of this reaches the package.
label_disclosure.body: Federal labeling law requires no disclosure of waste-management method. A cut of pork from a lagoon-and-sprayfield operation and one from a pasture-based operation carry identical mandatory label information. The environmental dimension is reachable only through two upstream FAT categories, neither of which appears on conventional pork.

categories.name: Farm / Ranch
categories.why: Waste-management method is a property of a specific farm. Without farm identity the question cannot be asked. Conventional pork discloses no farm.

categories.name: Who (corporate ownership)
categories.why: Siting and waste decisions are made by the integrator, not the grower whose name is on the mailbox. Conventional pork discloses no integrator — and DEQ's permit data carries no integrator field either.

categories.name: Supply-chain intermediaries
categories.why: The biogas joint venture is a second commercial channel monetizing the same waste stream. It appears in neither the meat's price nor its label.

label_disclosure.asymmetry: Verified, audited, government-certified disclosure exists in this system — it is simply pointed somewhere other than the consumer. California requires third-party verification of the carbon intensity of gas made from the waste. Neither the waste system nor the enforcement record is verified for, or disclosed to, the person buying the pork.

data_gaps.detail: NC DEQ's permit layer carries OWNER but no integrator or contractor field. Smithfield, Prestage and Murphy-Brown affiliation is absent from every DEQ source found. Any integrator mapping must come from secondary sources.

No NC DEQ lagoon or waste-structure GIS layer was found. DEQ's Agricultural_Operations layer is a spill and incident tracker, not structures. The only comprehensive NC lagoon geometry in public circulation is the Waterkeeper Alliance / Environmental Working Group aerial digitization, a third-party remote-sensing product, now dated.
NASS does not publish it in the quarterly series. Census of Agriculture (2022) is the alternative, at a different vintage and definition.
The 66 percent figure carried forward from the March 2026 map has no citation. Source it or remove it.
No DEQ publication states one. Figures in the 3,000 to 3,500 range circulate, including from industry sources, but do not trace to a state dataset.

data_gaps.gap: Swine-specific enforcement counts outside North Carolina
data_gaps.detail: No state in the top ten other than North Carolina publishes swine-specific inspection, complaint or violation counts. Indiana and Ohio publish all-species inspection tables; Iowa discloses counts to reporters on request; the rest publish none. See state_enforcement.

reproducible_queries.note: Run these against the NC DEQ feature service to refresh the nc_facility_counts block. Append to the layer URL in sources.nc_afo_layer.
reproducible_queries.filter_warning: Do not filter on PERMIT_EXPIRATION_DT > today. The 2019 general permits show an expiration of 2024-09-30 while remaining Active, because the replacements were extended to 2028-09-30 by S.L. 2025-97. Filter on PERMIT_STATUS instead.
